ergoweb.com — Force Guidelines – Ergoweb LLC — https://ergoweb.com/force-guidelines/
(found by the search; not opened or cited)
Elena Ruiz — Human Factors & Single-Operator Safety said about it: I take from Carts: Push/Pull Guidelines (E77) that sustained rolling force should drop to 25 pounds or less, from Force Guidelines – Ergoweb LLC (E78) that maximum two-handed sustained push-pull is 24 pounds, and from 3arm Solutions Help Manufacturers Maintain Safe Limits of Force Exertion (E80) that shoulder-height push is limited to 110 N, which all sit far below about 209 N pull and about 188 N hold from the tri-star climb over steps: cluster rotation and operator pull estimate (E23) with ratio about 1.45 from the ratio of downhill hold to female sustained pull limit (E59), about 19.2 kg in the hands from the hand-hold mass equivalent for 188 N stair hold (E83) like carrying a water crate all the way down, so the disc plus tooth hold at about 67.0 N m from the locked cluster holding torque and disc clamp on steep stair (E51) must carry it.
Elena Ruiz — Human Factors & Single-Operator Safety said about it: The numbers that decide it are total stair pull 209 N and total descent hold 188 N from the tri-star climb over steps cluster rotation and operator pull estimate (E23), against the sustained rolling limit of 25 pounds (lb) or 111 N when pushing more than 10 feet (ft) or for a minute I take from Carts Push Pull Guidelines (E77), and against the sustained two-handed push-pull limit of 24 lb or 107 N I take from Force Guidelines (E78), like holding a 19.2 kg bag from the hand-hold mass equivalent for 188 N stair hold (E83) on every step, so the tradeoff is that no handle leverage makes 188 N safe to hold and the spring-applied lock must carry it.
Elena Ruiz — Human Factors & Single-Operator Safety said about it: The numbers that decide it are total slope load 401 N from the slope load from total weight times sine theta (E97) needing total lock torque 74.2 N m from the total lock torque slope times cluster radius (E98), which needs 1.55 kN clamp from the clamp for corrected total torque (E100) superseding 1.40 kN in the locked cluster holding torque and disc clamp on steep stair (E51) because that used the lighter mass, giving 57.4 N finger force from the corrected hand release force (E101) with caliper ratio 8, lever ratio 4.5 and cable efficiency 0.75 including friction loss, against the maximum manual lever force of 29 lb or 129 N I take from Force Guidelines (E78), with factor 2.25, but above the 9 lb pinch limit so it needs a power grip at 3.8 to 6.4 centimetre (cm) span with wrist extension 25 degrees or less and neutral posture I take from Review of Hand/Wrist/Arm Ergonomics Analysis Methods (E56), and parked shear demand ratio 0.498 from the park pin shear with dynamic allowance (E102) for factor about 2.0 with impact allowance on the steepest slope, where Maximum Voluntary Contraction (MVC) fatigue rules say continuous grip above 10 percent (%) MVC is unacceptable from the same review, which is why hands-off auto-lock with no grip effort matters.
Elena Ruiz — Human Factors & Single-Operator Safety said about it: The numbers that decide it are total slope load 401 N from the slope load from total weight times sine theta (E97) needing total lock torque 74.2 N m from the total lock torque slope times cluster radius (E98), which needs 1.55 kN clamp from the clamp for corrected total torque (E100) because braking torque is pad force times friction times rotor radius I take from The Bicycle Physics of the Hydraulic Brake (E111), giving 57.4 N finger force from the corrected hand release force (E101) with caliper ratio 8, lever ratio 4.5 and cable efficiency 0.75 including friction loss, against maximum manual lever force 29 pounds (lb) I take from Force Guidelines (E78) with factor 2.25 but above maximum pinch force 9 lb, so it needs power grip at 3.8 to 6.4 centimetre span with wrist extension 25 degrees or less I take from Review of Hand/Wrist/Arm Ergonomics Analysis Methods: Part 1 (E56) where continuous grip above 10 percent of MVC is unacceptable, like lifting a 5.85 kg bag with two fingers, and parked shear demand ratio 0.498 from the park pin shear with dynamic allowance (E102) for factor about 2.0 with impact on the steepest slope.
Elena Ruiz — Human Factors & Single-Operator Safety said about it: I take from Force Guidelines (E78) that maximum manual lever force is 29 pounds and maximum pinch force is 9 pounds, and I take from The Bicycle Physics of the Hydraulic Brake (E111) that braking torque equals pad friction times clamp force times rotor radius.
Elena Ruiz — Human Factors & Single-Operator Safety said about it: The numbers that decide it are total lock 74.6 N m from the corrected lock torque with new weight (E124) needing 1.55 kN clamp from the clamp for corrected total torque (E100), giving 57.4 N finger force from the corrected hand release force (E101) with lever ratio 4.5 and cable efficiency 0.75 including friction loss, well within 129 N from Force Guidelines (E78) but above pinch so it needs power grip, like lifting a 5.85 kg bag with two fingers, and parked shear ratio 0.498 from the park pin shear with dynamic allowance (E102) for factor about 2.0 with impact, which checks as a spanner on a car nut not a finger hold.
